summary: portfolio-svc latency rose from about 120 ms to about 360 ms starting at 13:00 UTC, while error rate stayed flat (0.002-0.004, matching the report of no user errors). The earliest deviation is redis-cache's hit ratio, which fell below threshold from 12:58:49 and has sat at 0.88 since 13:02. The portfolio-svc deploy at 12:57 (described as a 'minor copy change') is the closest change before onset and is a candidate trigger, but I did not verify what it changed. Postgres summary metrics look healthy, so the extra latency is most likely cache misses on holdings reads rather than database saturation. I cannot separate a cache-key or behaviour change in the portfolio-svc deploy from a redis-side problem with the evidence gathered.

hypotheses.statement: redis-cache hit ratio degraded from about 12:58, so more portfolio-svc holdings reads miss the cache and are slower, which raised portfolio-svc latency from 13:00.
hypotheses.label: low

unresolved: Whether the portfolio-svc-00712 deploy actually changed cache behaviour is unverified; only its change note was seen.
Why the hit ratio began dropping at about 12:58 is unknown, so trigger and root cause are not separated.
The mechanism of the extra latency (database fall-through versus something else) is inferred, not measured.
Holdings cache-miss warnings in portfolio-svc began at 12:41 without any latency impact, and their relation to the later hit-ratio drop is unclear.
Postgres and redis metrics were checked only as whole-window summaries, not time series, so a small shift near 13:00 could be hidden.

actions.text: Diff portfolio-svc-00712 for changes to cache keys, TTLs or holdings read paths. If anything cache-related changed, roll it back.
actions.rationale: It is the closest change before the hit-ratio drop and the latency step, and the 'copy change' label may understate what changed.

actions.text: Check redis-cache for what is missing: key patterns, TTL or expiry behaviour, and any flush or restart around 12:58. Also check whether redis-cache-00897 changed anything beyond the log level.
actions.rationale: The hit ratio fell without evictions or memory pressure, so the cause is likely key churn, expiry or a client-side change.

actions.text: Check postgres per-query load from portfolio-svc holdings queries over 12:55-13:30 to confirm the misses are falling through to the database.
actions.rationale: Summary metrics look healthy, but a time-series view would confirm or rule out the fall-through mechanism.
